risk_narrative:
**CONFIDENTIAL**

**Executive Risk Narrative — Engagement eng-20260830165108-web-audit-v2-proof**

The security assessment covering 2 assets and 5 endpoints identified 29 total findings, of which 2 are rated Critical and 6 are rated High — a concentration of severe risk within a limited attack surface that warrants immediate executive attention. Both Critical findings affect the Redis deployment: an integer overflow in Lua script handling (versions prior to 8.2.1) and a use-after-free condition in the Lua parser (prior to 8.2.2). These are memory-corruption class vulnerabilities that, depending on exposure, could enable remote code execution or denial of service against the data layer. This is compounded by a High-severity cross-user Lua sandbox escape (prior to 8.2.2), which undermines isolation boundaries and could allow one context to access another user's data or execution environment. The clustering of these flaws in a shared infrastructure component means a single compromised Redis instance represents a high-value pivot point across the environment.

At the application layer, two High-severity SQL injection vulnerabilities were confirmed via the POST `password` parameter, identified through differential analysis. Injection on an authentication path is particularly consequential: it may permit authentication bypass, exposure of credential stores, or broader database compromise, and it directly threatens the confidentiality and integrity of user accounts. The remaining findings (1 Medium, 20 Informational) reflect normal assessment noise, but the overall severity density — 8 of 29 findings rated High or Critical across only 5 endpoints — indicates an elevated risk posture. We recommend prioritized remediation: upgrade Redis to 8.2.2 or later as the immediate action, remediate the SQL injection flaws through parameterized queries and input validation, and verify the effectiveness of any compensating controls (WAF rules, network segmentation) in the interim. A focused retest should follow remediation to confirm closure of the Critical and High findings.

top_findings.title: Redis Lua Sandbox < 8.2.2 - Cross-User Escape
top_findings.description: Redis is an open source, in-memory database that persists on disk. Versions 8.2.1 and below allow an authenticated user to use a specially crafted Lua script to manipulate different LUA objects and potentially run their own code in the context of another user. The problem exists in all versions of Redis with LUA scripting. This issue is fixed in version 8.2.2. A workaround to mitigate the problem without patching the redis-server executable is to prevent users from executing LUA scripts. This can be done using ACL to block a script by restricting both the EVAL and FUNCTION command families.
